scope: Independent source review only; no implementation edits, test run, or live browser exercise.

verdict_a_acceptance.source_assessment: Chrome manifest declares debugger required and the Settings row has no switch; optional Chrome grants are requested and removed through the permissions API, with false and thrown request/remove results shown to the user. Live Chrome retest remains required.
missing: Firefox and Safari manifests filter out pageCapture and tabCapture, but the shared ALL_OPTIONAL list still renders both switches in Advanced agent capabilities. An admin can attempt a grant that this extension build cannot supply.
The dispatcher still describes debugger as an optional permission and directs the agent to a nonexistent Settings toggle if its required-permission check fails.

findings.title: Permission roster is not build-specific
findings.evidence: wxt.config.ts:118-120 removes pageCapture and tabCapture from Firefox/Safari optional_permissions, while src/lib/permissions/optional.ts:57-68,92-94 and AdvancedAgentCapabilities.tsx:99-123 always render them as actionable switches.
findings.effect: A browser-specific build presents unsupported capabilities as grantable and retries cannot repair the manifest mismatch. Filter the roster by the actual build capability or manifest.

findings.title: Refresh rejection can strand a switch busy
findings.evidence: AdvancedAgentCapabilities.tsx:67-70 awaits refresh() before setBusy(null), and refresh() calls permissions.contains without catch at lines 44-50.
findings.effect: If contains rejects after a grant or removal result, the async handler rejects and the switch stays disabled. Make state cleanup unconditional and show a recoverable status-read error.

findings.title: Debugger gate gives impossible remediation
findings.evidence: src/lib/tools/dispatch.ts:781-789 applies the optional-permission error to required_optional_permissions including debugger, telling the agent to enable an Advanced agent capabilities toggle; the new UI intentionally has none.
findings.effect: In a build where debugger is absent, the tool failure points to an action the user cannot take.

findings.title: New tests omit grant denial, thrown API results, and status-read failure
findings.evidence: tests/unit/advanced-agent-capabilities.test.tsx:44-92 covers debugger status, successful removal, and false removal only; no grant-denial or rejection path is asserted.
findings.effect: The stated recoverability contract is only partly guarded. No live proof or mutation/gut-check evidence was provided with the implementation report.

verdict_b_engineering_quality.positive_evidence: RuntimeOptionalPermission excludes debugger from request/remove signatures; Chrome documentation forbids debugger as optional and says removing required permissions returns false. The tests do exercise the key no-switch and false-removal behaviors.

open_questions: Retest actual Chrome Settings grant, removal, refusal, and reload behavior before acceptance closure.
